name: Home Renovation Savings — Home Energy Assessment path
runBy: Enbridge Gas + Save on Energy (IESO), with Ontario government support
auditRequirementNote: Requires an initial and a follow-up EnerGuide home energy assessment by an NRCan-registered energy advisor, plus at least two eligible upgrades.
headline: Get $600 back on your energy assessments — then up to $7,700 for insulation
whoQualifies: Ontario homeowners completing two or more eligible upgrades. The program sends you a list of service organizations only after you submit a contact form — or you can compare providers openly here.
notes: The assessment typically costs $500–$900 + HST across both visits, so the $600 rebate covers most of it. The same registered advisor must do the initial and follow-up visits.

name: Home Renovation Savings — direct rebates (no assessment)
auditRequirementNote: No EnerGuide assessment needed for this stream.
headline: Heat pump and single-upgrade rebates without an assessment

amounts.label: Cold-climate heat pump
amounts.value: up to $12,000 (varies by current heating type)

whoQualifies: Ontario homeowners doing a single eligible upgrade through a participating contractor.
notes: Even where no assessment is required, an audit-first approach usually changes what you buy — right-sized heat pumps and insulation-first sequencing typically save more than equipment alone.

name: Toronto Home Energy Loan Program (HELP)
auditRequirementNote: A home energy assessment with an NRCan-registered energy advisor is required for most projects. Exception: heat-pump-only and rooftop-solar-only projects.
headline: Low-interest City loans up to $125,000 for home energy retrofits
whoQualifies: Toronto homeowners. 20-year terms are limited to solar, geothermal, window, or heat pump projects.
notes: Stacks with Home Renovation Savings rebates — a common path is HELP financing + HRSP rebates + the $600 assessment rebate.

name: CMHC Eco Improvement premium refund
auditRequirementNote: An EnerGuide evaluation isn't mandatory, but submitting an EnerGuide Renovation Upgrade Report or label strengthens your claim.
headline: 25% back on your CMHC mortgage insurance premium after energy renovations
whoQualifies: Buyers with CMHC-insured mortgages who complete eligible envelope, mechanical, or renewable upgrades after purchase.
notes: Often missed by recent buyers. Sagen and Canada Guaranty offer comparable programs — ask your broker.

name: Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program
runBy: Natural Resources Canada with provincial delivery partners
auditRequirementNote: The program arranges its own assessments and retrofits — you don't choose the advisor.
headline: No-cost retrofits for income-qualified households — not yet delivering in Ontario
whoQualifies: Low-to-median-income homeowners and tenants in participating provinces: BC, Manitoba, Nova Scotia, PEI, and Quebec as of July 2026. Ontario delivery has not been announced.
notes: We'll update this the day Ontario delivery is announced.

name: Canada Greener Homes Grant
auditRequirementNote: Required EnerGuide evaluations while it ran.
headline: Closed — stopped accepting new applications in February 2024
whoQualifies: Closed to new applicants. Over 409,000 households completed it.
notes: Many sites still advertise this program. It is closed — don't let anyone sell you an audit on the promise of this grant.

name: Canada Greener Homes Loan
auditRequirementNote: Required EnerGuide evaluations while it ran.
headline: Closed — new applications ended October 1, 2025 (funding fully committed)
whoQualifies: Closed to new applicants. Already-approved loans are unaffected.
notes: Closed with roughly two weeks' notice — a reminder to act while programs are open.

name: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability Program
auditRequirementNote: EnerGuide evaluation was not always required.
headline: Closed to new applications July 31, 2026
whoQualifies: Closed. Existing participants have until January 31, 2027 to submit documents.

name: Home Efficiency Rebate Plus (HER+)
auditRequirementNote: Required EnerGuide evaluations while it ran.
headline: Ended — replaced by Home Renovation Savings in January 2025
whoQualifies: Closed. If a site is advertising HER+, its information is out of date.
